mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior 6 months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q-o-q for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) predicts weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 y-o-y < -2% AND HOUST falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP/starts co-move positively during a tech-driven rally.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a strong productivity rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months, accompanied by a fall in capacity utilization (implied by INDPRO and RSAFS), signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower earnings visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a tech or services-led expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency easing, which immediately boosts risk asset valuations through lower borrowing costs, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls >1% in one month to below 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered events, or the mechanism fails outside of crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered recoveries, or the mechanism fails during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained period where CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% while the federal funds rate remains below 2% for three consecutive months signals a negative real policy rate environment, which stimulates equity valuations through lower effective discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a sharp rise in risk premia.
